Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly implements national-scale, spatially explicit land-use and land-cover (LULC) modeling across Brazil using the GLOBIOM-Brazil model at ~50 km resolution. Its primary objective is to simulate future LULC change (specifically deforestation, pasture, cropland, and native vegetation dynamics) under multiple policy scenarios of Brazil’s Forest Code through 2050. It compares ≥2 quantitative future scenarios (e.g., FC vs. NoFC, IDCAmazon, IDCImperfect variants, etc.), reports mapped spatial projections (Figures 1–5), and provides quantitative metrics such as area changes in million hectares, deforestation rates, and model validation against historical data (e.g., 16.45 Mha projected vs. 16.53 Mha observed 2001–2010). The study meets all core inclusion criteria and avoids all exclusion criteria—it is not global-only, not regional/local, includes explicit future LULC prediction as its central focus, and produces spatially explicit national projections with accuracy assessment.)
